description: Fig. 12 is a four-panel composite of SEM secondary-electron fractographs of rolled Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe tensile specimens: (a) 0Be, (b) 0.5Be, (c) 1.0Be, (d) 1.5Be. Each panel pairs a high-magnification view of the fracture surface with a small inset macro-photograph of the whole broken specimen (1 mm scale bar) in which a white square marks the region enlarged, labelled "Area A1", "Area B1", "Area C1" and "Area D1". Panel (a) has a 25 µm scale bar; (b), (c) and (d) have 50 µm scale bars. (a) is dominated by a rough ductile fibrous zone with many dimples, and a red ellipse labelled "Area A2" on the ~1 mm inset marks the macro fracture region where dissociation planes and river patterns appear; the cited text states spherical inclusions are evident in the dimples of area A1. From (b) to (d) the surfaces become progressively flatter, (c) and (d) showing broad flat facets and cleavage platforms; (d) carries red text "Cleavage steps" with two red arrows pointing to step-like ridges, plus an unlabelled blue arrow. The group demonstrates a ductile-to-more-cleavage fracture transition with increasing Be content.

observations.observation: The figure contains four SEM tensile fracture-surface micrographs labelled (a) 0Be, (b) 0.5Be, (c) 1.0Be and (d) 1.5Be.
Panel (a) carries a 25 µm scale bar, while panels (b), (c) and (d) each carry a 50 µm scale bar.

Each panel contains a low-magnification inset photograph of the whole fractured specimen with a 1 mm scale bar and a white square marking the enlarged area, labelled Area A1, Area B1, Area C1 and Area D1 respectively.
In panel (a) a red ellipse labelled 'Area A2' marks the macro fracture region in the 1 mm inset, while the white square 'Area A1' sits at the upper right.
Panel (a) shows a ductile fibrous fracture surface covered in dimples, with the raised/rough relief typical of a fibre zone.
Panel (d) is annotated with red text 'Cleavage steps' and two red arrows pointing to step-like ridges, plus an additional unlabelled blue arrow.
From (b) to (d) the fracture surfaces become progressively flatter, with broad facets and cleavage platforms appearing in (c) and (d).
The caption states the figure is the SEM tensile fracture morphology of (a) 0Be, (b) 0.5Be, (c) 1.0Be and (d) 1.5Be steels.

The citing text reports that area A1 at the upper right of Fig. 12(a) is an enlarged view and that spherical inclusions are more evident in the dimples of the ductile fibre area, and that dissociation planes and river patterns appear in the macro fracture area A2.
The citing text states the dissociation surface at fracture of 1.0Be and 1.5Be steels gradually increases and that cleavage platforms appear in Fig. 12(c–d).
The citing text states that the figure shows rolled Fe-30Mn–10Al–1.5C-xBe steels tested in tension.
No numeric stress, strain or inclusion-size values are printed on any panel; the only numerical annotations are the scale bars (25 µm, 50 µm, 1 mm).

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of the 0Be steel, 25 µm scale bar, showing a rough fibrous fracture surface densely covered with dimples; inset macro-photograph (1 mm scale bar) shows the whole specimen with a white square labelled 'Area A1' (enlarged region) and a red ellipse labelled 'Area A2' over the macro fracture area.

SEM fractograph of the 0.5Be steel, 50 µm scale bar, showing an uneven dimpled, largely ductile fracture surface with fine tear ridges; inset specimen photograph (1 mm scale bar) with white square labelled 'Area B1'.

SEM fractograph of the 1.0Be steel, 50 µm scale bar, showing dimples mixed with flatter, quasi-cleavage-like facets and shallow platforms; inset specimen photograph (1 mm scale bar) with white square labelled 'Area C1'.

SEM fractograph of the 1.5Be steel, 50 µm scale bar, showing a comparatively flat surface with large facets, cleavage-like platforms and step ridges; red text 'Cleavage steps' with two red arrows pointing to step features and an additional unlabelled blue arrow; inset specimen photograph (1 mm scale bar) with white square labelled 'Area D1'.
